title: Generating Vector-Vortex $γ$ Photons by Nonlinear Compton Scattering
authors: Yong-Zheng Ren, Mamutjan Ababekri, Jun-Lin Zhou, Feng Wan, Qian Zhao, Zhong-Peng Li, Kun Xue, Ya-Qing Huang, Zhao-Hui Chen, Zhong-Feng Xu, Jian-Xing Li
abstract: Vector-vortex photons, characterized by a nonseparable coupling between polarization and orbital angular momentum (OAM), offer opportunities for optical manipulation, quantum communication, nuclear photonics, etc. However, their generation in the $γ$-ray regime remains challenging. Here, we put forward a novel method to generate vector-vortex $γ$ photons via nonlinear Compton scattering in elliptically polarized laser pulses. We reveal that tailoring laser ellipticity directs the multiphoton absorption to coherently populate OAM modes with opposite winding numbers, $\pm \ell$, tied to orthogonal circular polarizations, producing nonseparable spin-OAM photon states. For a linearly polarized laser of moderate intensity (dimensionless amplitude $a_0 \sim 1$), the mode-pair concurrence--a 0-to-1 measure of spin-OAM entanglement--reaches unity for MeV $γ$ photons, realizing maximally nonseparable radial- or azimuthal-type vector-vortex states. The laser amplitude further controls the accessible OAM spectrum. Our method offers a route to MeV vector-vortex photons, opening a new avenue for nuclear-scale structured photonics and high-energy quantum information.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical method to generate highly structured vector-vortex gamma photons via nonlinear Compton scattering using elliptically polarized lasers. By controlling the laser's ellipticity, the authors demonstrate the ability to achieve maximal spin-OAM entanglement in the resulting high-energy photons. This opens a new avenue for utilizing structured light concepts in nuclear-scale photonics and high-energy quantum information.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the generation of vector-vortex gamma photons, which are structured light states exhibiting a nonseparable coupling between polarization and orbital angular momentum (OAM), particularly in the high-energy gamma-ray regime.
main_result: The authors propose a novel mechanism using nonlinear Compton scattering (NCS) with elliptically polarized lasers, demonstrating that the mode-pair concurrence can reach unity for MeV gamma photons, realizing maximally nonseparable vector-vortex states.
method: The analysis involves calculating the leading-order S-matrix element for NCS, projecting the emitted photon state onto a Bessel photon mode, and quantifying the spin-OAM entanglement using mode-pair concurrence.
model_or_system: The physical system is the nonlinear Compton scattering process where an ultrarelativistic electron beam interacts head-on with an elliptically polarized laser pulse. The theoretical framework utilizes the Furry picture and Volkov states.
key_observables: Mode-pair concurrence (measure of spin-OAM entanglement), energy–angle resolved probability density ($d^2W_{VV}$), and HOPS coordinates.
important_parameters: Laser ellipticity ($\epsilon$), laser amplitude ($a_0$), and the resulting gamma-ray energy (MeV).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the non-spin-flip channel ($\lambda' = \lambda$), which dominates in the moderate-field regime ($a_0 \sim 1$), and assumes an ultrarelativistic NCS geometry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how laser ellipticity controls the photon state on the Higher-Order Poincaré Sphere (HOPS), showing transitions from scalar-vortex to vector-vortex states, and display energy-angle probability distributions for selected vector-vortex modes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by calculating the scattering amplitude, analyzing the resulting photon state in a Bessel basis, and then demonstrating the control mechanism by tuning laser ellipticity ($\epsilon$) to maximize the spin-OAM concurrence.
why_interesting: This work bridges high-energy quantum electrodynamics (QED) with structured light concepts, providing a pathway to engineer quantum states of light at MeV energies, which is highly relevant for advanced quantum optics and high-energy physics applications.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Generation of vector-vortex γ photons via NCS. A relativistic electron beam collides head-on with an arbitrarily polarized laser field, whose RCP and LCP components are shown in the inset. Laser ellipticity controls their relative weights and hence the photon state on the higher-order Poincar´e sphere (HOPS): circular polarization favors scalar-vortex states near the poles (b,e), whereas an LP drive balances the two helicity pathways and yields equatorial vector-vortex states, including radial-type (f), azimuthal-type (c), and hybrid modes (a,d). Each HOPS panel shows transverse phase (left) and intensity (right), with arrows indicating the local polarization.

FIG. 2. Transverse intensity and polarization distributions of representative vector-vortex γ-photon modes |Vm,δ⟩defined in Eq. (2). Panels (a)-(e) show the radial-type modes (δ = 0), while panels (f)-(j) show the corresponding azimuthal-type modes (δ = π), with mode orders m = −3, −2, −1, 1, and 2. The color maps represent the normalized transverse intensity distributions in the transverse coordinate plane, while the black arrows indicate the local linear-polarization directions. Insets show the corresponding transverse phase distributions. These normalized profiles illustrate the analyzer basis and do not represent calculated NCS emission distributions.

FIG. 3. Laser-ellipticity dependence of the integrated probabilities and interference magnitude for different vector-vortex mode orders m. The blue and orange bars show P(m, 0) and P(m, π) for the radial- and azimuthal-type analyzers, respectively, while the yellow bars show the interference magnitude Im. All quantities are integrated over 0 ≤ω′ ≤36 MeV and 0 ≤θk′ ≤2.5 mrad. Panels (a)–(e) correspond to ϵ = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and 1, respectively. The percentages above the bars denote the concurrence Cm of the corresponding mode pair.

FIG. 4. Laser-intensity dependence of the integrated probabilities and interference magnitude for different vector-vortex mode orders m, for an LP laser field (ϵ = 0). The blue and orange bars show P(m, 0) and P(m, π) for the radial- and azimuthal-type analyzers, respectively, while the yellow bars show the interference magnitude Im. The same energy–angle integration window as in Fig. 3 is used. Panels (a)–(d) correspond to a0 = 0.1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively. The percentages above the bars denote the concurrence Cm of the corresponding mode pair.

FIG. 5. Energy–angle probability-density distributions for selected radial-type (m = −3, −1, 1) and azimuthal-type (m = −2, 2) vector-vortex γ-photon modes produced via NCS in an LP laser field. Note that the color-bar scale differs among panels.
